questions.q: -rw-r----- 1 root bazaar .env. Who can read it?
options: root (the owner) and members of the bazaar group
questions.explain: Owner rw-, group r--, others ---. That's mode 640: the right setting for Bazaar's .env.

questions.q: .env is 600 (rw-------), owned by root, group bazaar. Asha is in bazaar. Can she read it?
options: No: the kernel uses only the group bits for her, and they are ---
questions.explain: The kernel picks exactly one set (owner, group or others) and never falls through to another.
7 = rwx (4+2+1), 5 = r-x (4+1). Owner can do everything; group and others can read and run.

questions.q: Ravi can't write root_report.txt (it's read-only), but he deleted it. How?
options: Deleting removes a name from the folder, so it needs w on the folder, and the folder was 777
questions.explain: A file's name lives in its folder. The sticky bit (like on /tmp) stops deleting other people's files.

questions.q: A folder is rwx--x--x (711). What can others do?
options: Not list it, but open a file inside if they know its exact name
questions.explain: On a folder, r = list names, x = enter and reach things by name, w = create/delete names.

questions.q: Nginx shows 403 Forbidden for product photos. What's the right fix?
options: Check which user Nginx runs as, then give it read on the photos and x on every folder on the way
Delete the photos and upload them again
questions.explain: 777 lets anyone change anything. Grant exactly the missing permission; namei -l shows every folder on the path.

questions.q: Why is sudo better than logging in as root?
options: It runs only the one command as root, asks for your own password, and records who ran what
questions.explain: Least privilege: work as a normal user, and use sudo only for commands that need root.

questions.q: (Going deeper) With the usual umask 022, what permissions does a new file get?
questions.explain: Files start from 666 and lose the umask bits: 666 − 022 = 644. Folders: 777 − 022 = 755.
